changes.before: Initialize message with std::string{"ready"} instead of 7. What prints?
changes.after: Store one of several allowed types and check which type is active.

before: std::variant<int,std::string> normally owns one of those two alternatives at a time. Assigning a string replaces the int alternative; it does not retain both payloads.
std::get_if<int>(&message) returns a pointer to the int when it is active, otherwise nullptr. The if checks that pointer before dereferencing it.

std::get<T> throws std::bad_variant_access for the wrong active alternative. This example’s else knows the other alternative because these simple assignments succeed. A variant can become valueless after certain throwing operations; general code must account for that possibility.
Expected output or behavior: number 7. Local compiler test evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Add a visitor that formats either alternative, then compare it with the get_if branch. You may trace this without a compiler; finishing the reading is not proof of a local run.
after: std::variant<int, std::string> can hold an integer or a string. The type currently held is called the active alternative. It normally holds one alternative at a time, not both.
std::get_if<int>(&message) checks for the integer alternative. It returns a pointer to that integer when present, or nullptr otherwise. The if condition checks the pointer before *number reads it.

std::get<T> reads the requested alternative or throws std::bad_variant_access if that alternative is not active. Here the successful initialization leaves either an int or a string, so the else branch can read the string.
The program prints number 7. message holds an int, so get_if returns a valid pointer and the first branch reads seven.
Some operations that throw while replacing an alternative can leave a variant without a value. General code may need to check valueless_by_exception(). This example performs no such replacement.

before.question: Initialize message with std::string{"ready"} instead of 7. What prints?

after.question: Initialize message with std::string{"ready"} instead of 7. What prints?
after.explanation: The string alternative is active. get_if<int> returns nullptr, so the else branch reads the string.
